home.title: Declare the domain, then derive the layers that use it.
home.subtitle: One entity class, and from it: the validator that runs in the browser and at the façade, the SQLite table, the form contract, the REST and GraphQL surfaces. Because the declaration is JSON on the wire, the domain can move to its own process — the calling code does not change.
home.gradientText: A Frond runs inside the application by default. Add its address to remotes to route the same calls through JSON-RPC 2.0. Local calls remain in-memory calls.
home.statAxesText: each field states its shape, role, lifecycle and boundary — every adapter reads them
home.statPrimitivesText: useQuery, useCommand, useFormFor, useCurrentUser, and invoke
home.dogfoodText: The blog uses a Frond with a Post entity and a publish operation. Its pages use useQuery, useCommand, and useFormFor. Authentication uses the better-auth adapter; documentation is managed separately by Nuxt Content.
home.realCode: The code below is this site's own blog Frond — not pseudocode.
home.declareText: Define fields and their rules in one class. Fougere provides validation, the SQLite table, the GraphQL type, and the form contract.
home.judgeText: Handlers apply business rules. readOnly prevents the client from changing a server-managed field.
home.consumeText: Import the class into a page. useQuery reads data; useCommand changes it and refreshes queries linked to the entity.
home.gradientPoint1: Remote calls preserve the error code, message, and per-field details
home.gradientPoint2: The server sends session state to remote collectors
home.gradientPoint3: An unavailable host produces a typed error, mapped to HTTP 503 in Nuxt
home.foreignText: The remote contract uses JSON-RPC 2.0 and rpc.discover, which describes the available operations and schemas. The demos/rust-frond directory contains an implementation of this contract in Rust.
home.foreignAxes: The client reconstructs the received schema and validates the request before the call. JSON Schema describes field shapes; x-fougere extensions carry their role, lifecycle and boundary.
home.foreignCaption: TypeScript validation using rules published by the Rust demo
home.derivationText: An entity describes the model. Fougere derives validation, storage, forms, and APIs from it.
home.compareTitle: Fewer declarations to keep in sync
home.compareText: Without a shared source, the same fields get declared in the validator, the table, the endpoint and the form — four files that must never drift. Fougere derives all four from the entity.
home.compareBeforeLabel: The same structure declared in 4 files
home.auditText: This prompt asks an agent to find repeated structures and the code that keeps them synchronized. It also asks for an estimate of the cost of adopting Fougere.
home.statTopologyText: remotes.blog provides the address of a remotely executed Frond
home.statusText: Fougere is in pre-release. These scenarios are implemented and tested in the repository:
home.status1: The five client primitives are used by the Nuxt demo
home.status2: The blog covers creating, editing, and publishing a post
home.status3: An unavailable remote host returns a typed error
home.status4: Calls are tested with local and remote execution, including after a production build
home.status5: This site's blog and authentication use Fougere
